text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert is against more say for works councils as they may deter investment. (p1)
- Building group BAM is to take over Dutch operations of Wilma International. (p1)
- Food and drinks combine BolsWessanen soon to take over a U.S. distributor of specialty food. (p1)
- Slaughter houses fight over for the scarse supply of pigs due to swine fever epidemic. (p1)
- Building and trading concern NBM Amstelland takes over network firm Van den Berg from the ULC Groep. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell sees oil and gas reserves grow for the the first fime since 1992. (p1)
- Schiphol Airport to participate in possible development of industrial sites around Teeside airport, northeast England.(p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Workers' unions and employers' association sign draft agreement on demotion for older employees. (p1)
- Parliament wants to stop profiteering with options in own company. (p1)
- Dutch industrial output in February up five pct from same period last year. (p2)
- Antonov, UK developer of small car automatic gearboxes, seeks a listing on Amsterdam Exchanges' New Market NMAX. (p15) DE TELEGRAAF
- Ministry of transport has plans to allow trucks with a total length of 25 metres on the road. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM bans pate de foie gras from its flights' menu. (p7)
- Cabinet puts aside 280 million guilders for some dozen projects aimed at cutting carbon-dioxide exhaust emissions. (p8)
- Mortgage supplier Huis & Hypotheek wants the Rabobank to change similar name for its mortgage unit. (p25)
TROUW
- European Commission starts official investigation into Dutch state support of Philips and Rabobank through technical lease construction. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers wants solar energy technology to become a Dutch export product. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Association of vegetable and fruit exporters investigate possibility of testcase against monopoly position of auction group The Greenery. (p10)
- Bank-insurer ING's insurance unit seeks to extend its distribution network in Argentina. (p11)
